A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same UltraFusion paper. All 11 pages were checked, including text, equations, tables, figures, and references. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix. The only difference is the first-page arXiv version/date stamp.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original benchmark evaluations, component ablations, qualitative demonstrations, and a user study with 136 participants (Tables 1–3 and Figure 5).

after.justification: Section 4 retains the same original benchmark results, ablations, qualitative demonstrations, and user-study outcomes (Tables 1–3 and Figure 5).

M1.justification: Section 3 retains identical RAFT pre-alignment, occlusion masking, and diffusion-based guided inpainting with the decompose-and-fuse control branch. No algorithm or model component changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate on MEFB, RealHDRV, and the captured UltraFusion benchmark. The represented exposure and motion scenarios and the general image-fusion demonstration in Section 4.4 are unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership matches within every comparison: the same ten baselines in Table 1 and six in Table 2. The ControlNet comparisons and ablations are also unchanged.

E3.justification: Sections 4.1–4.2 preserve the dataset sizes, training budget, evaluation metrics, input construction, and Photomatix tone mapping. Both report the same user-study design using 20 scenes and 136 participants.

E4.justification: The component-removal ablations and analyses of structure guidance, color guidance, and cross-attention are identical in Section 4.3, Table 3, and Figures 10–11. The qualitative comparison cases also match.

E5.justification: Both retain identical point-estimate tables and user-preference bars. Neither reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical entries, plotted findings, and qualitative examples match. For example, UltraFusion's MEFB MUSIQ remains 68.82 in Table 1, and its RealHDRV TMQI remains 0.8925 in Table 2.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(2), specifying masked warping and luminance normalization, and their mathematical explanations are identical. No formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about fusion across exposure differences up to nine stops, robustness to alignment errors and motion, guided inpainting, and the UltraFusion benchmark.

C2.justification: Both retain the same quality–fidelity interpretation and limitations. Section 5 still explains that erroneous occlusion masks can remove useful guidance, leaving unreliable highlight restoration from diffusion priors.

D1.justification: Implementation disclosures remain identical: Stable Diffusion V2.1, 140k iterations, batch size 32, eight RTX 4090 GPUs, and Adam with learning rate 0.0001. Project and demo access statements are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 and all 68 bibliography entries are identical. Positioning relative to HDR reconstruction, multi-exposure fusion, diffusion models, and tone mapping is unchanged.

P1.justification: Only the marginal arXiv stamp changes from v1, dated 20 January 2025, to v2, dated 1 March 2025. The title, authors, body wording, terminology, and section structure are identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1–12, Tables 1–3, captions, and page layout are unchanged. Rendered-page differences are confined to the marginal version/date text recorded under P1.

improvement.justification: The later PDF changes only the arXiv version/date stamp. Scientific content, empirical evidence, reproducibility information, limitations, and substantive presentation are identical, establishing no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
